purpose: Plan, evaluate, prioritize, and execute the work units of building an audience with content: niche and persona, value loop and community, hooks and retention, platform algorithm and format fit, discovery, and the short/long/series/live formats, as evaluable session-bounded steps for a knowledge-searcher meta-KB.
assumptions: subdomain of Creator Craft & Content Production, scoped to content and audience strategy for social-influencer audience-building
nodes are concrete content/audience-strategy work units, methods, and decision areas
no observed dataset supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors
platform algorithm behavior is modeled heuristically and is assumed to drift over time
the creator is building, not yet operating at scale; capacity is a real constraint
exclusions: video/audio editing craft and production tooling specifics
monetization mechanics (ad rates, sponsorship deals, pricing)
legal, brand-safety, and platform-policy compliance detail
personal-brand visual identity and graphic design execution

competency_questions.question: What niche and target audience is this channel built for and is the demand real?
Who is the specific viewer, what problem do they have, and what words do they use?
What repeatable promise does each piece keep and why does a viewer return, subscribe, and join the community?
What recurring content pillars and series cover the niche and map to audience problems?
How is the first-seconds hook and title/thumbnail designed to earn the start?
How is each piece structured and re-edited from the retention curve to carry attention to the end?
What sustainable publishing cadence and repurposing system keep output consistent without burnout?
How does the target platform's recommendation algorithm decide what to surface?
How is content adapted to each platform's native format and ranking signals?
When should the creator participate in a trend versus stay on evergreen pillars?
How is content optimized for platform and external search discovery?
Which format (short-form, long-form, series, live) fits a given goal and how is it produced?
How are passive viewers converted into an interacting community and into subscribers, signups, or revenue?
How does the measurement loop turn reach, retention, and conversion data into the next iteration, and what checks gate publishing?

glossary.definition: the focused topic-and-audience intersection a channel commits to
a concrete profile of the target viewer's problem, language, and habits
the repeatable promise plus reason-to-return that compounds subscribers
a recurring theme that organizes the content backlog
the first seconds or packaging that earns the viewer's choice to start
the watch-time graph showing where viewers drop off
the sustainable rhythm at which content is published
alignment of content and packaging to a platform's ranking signals
matching aspect, length, and pacing to a platform's native format
a timely sound, format, or topic with a short reach window
optimizing metadata for search-driven, evergreen surfacing
the explicit next step that converts attention into an action

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established content/audience-strategy literature (Kawasaki & Fitzpatrick 2014, The Art of Social Media; Kleon 2014, Show Your Work!) and creator-growth practice; no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible
platform algorithm behavior is modeled heuristically and changes over time

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Choose a defensible content niche at the intersection of creator interest, audience demand, and monetizable demand.
contradictors: generalist posting on everything

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when demand signals or competitive landscape shift materially

pros.claim: the whole channel inherits one focused, searchable identity
pros.example: a fitness-for-busy-parents niche beats generic fitness

cons.claim: a wrong niche wastes months of compounding before it shows
cons.example: posting broad lifestyle content that never builds a returning audience

failure_modes: niche chosen by passion only, ignoring demand
niche too broad to rank or be remembered
acceptance_tests: niche stated in one sentence naming audience and transformation
at least one demand signal cited, not assumed

nodes.definition: Build a concrete persona of the target viewer including their problem, language, and the platforms they already use.
contradictors: creator who pictures only themselves as the viewer

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the actual audience analytics diverge from the assumed persona

pros.claim: downstream hooks and topics speak the viewer's real language
pros.example: using the audience's own phrasing in titles lifts click-through

cons.claim: a fictional persona makes every hook land slightly off
cons.example: writing for experts when the audience are anxious beginners

failure_modes: persona invented, not evidenced
persona ignores where the audience actually watches
acceptance_tests: persona names a specific problem the viewer says out loud
persona is grounded in at least one real data source

nodes.definition: Define the repeatable promise each piece keeps and the loop that turns a viewer into a returning subscriber.
contradictors: creator chasing one-off viral hits with no return loop

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when subscriber conversion or return rate drops below plan

pros.claim: one consistent promise makes subscribing a rational choice
pros.example: a new productivity system every Tuesday gives a reason to return

cons.claim: no return loop means the audience never compounds
cons.example: high views but flat subscriber growth

failure_modes: promise differs every video, so no expectation forms
value framed as the creator's interest, not the viewer's gain
acceptance_tests: the promise is statable in one sentence and kept every piece
there is an explicit reason the viewer returns

nodes.definition: Define 3-5 recurring content themes that cover the niche and map to audience problems and search demand.
contradictors: creator posting random unconnected topics

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a pillar consistently underperforms or audience interest shifts

pros.claim: pillars turn a vague niche into a plannable, repeatable backlog
pros.example: three pillars feed a quarter of videos without idea drought

cons.claim: too many pillars dilute identity and confuse the algorithm
cons.example: a channel that is part cooking, part finance, part vlog

failure_modes: pillars overlap and become indistinguishable
pillars chosen without demand evidence
acceptance_tests: each pillar maps to a stated audience problem
pillar count is small enough to stay recognizable

nodes.definition: Engineer the first seconds (or title and thumbnail) so a scrolling viewer chooses to start and stay.
contradictors: creator who buries the point after a long intro

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when click-through or early-retention metrics fall

pros.claim: the strongest content is invisible without a hook that earns the start
pros.example: a sharper first line doubles average view duration

cons.claim: an over-promising hook spikes clicks but tanks retention and trust
cons.example: clickbait that the video never pays off

failure_modes: hook over-promises and the body underdelivers
intro too slow for the platform's scroll speed
acceptance_tests: the hook names the payoff in the first seconds
title/thumbnail promise matches what the content delivers

nodes.definition: Structure each piece with narrative tension, stakes, and payoff so attention is carried to the end.
contradictors: creator who lists facts with no through-line

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when mid-video retention dips appear in the curve

pros.claim: narrative tension is what keeps a viewer past the hook
pros.example: a setup-payoff loop holds viewers through a long explainer

cons.claim: story added for its own sake can pad and lose impatient viewers
cons.example: a two-minute personal anecdote before any value

failure_modes: no through-line connects the segments
open loops are never paid off
acceptance_tests: each segment advances one through-line
every open loop has a payoff

nodes.definition: Read retention and watch-time curves to locate drop-offs and re-edit pacing, segment order, and density.
contradictors: creator who never looks at the retention graph

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a recurring drop-off pattern appears across pieces

pros.claim: the curve shows exactly where attention is lost, removing guesswork
pros.example: cutting a slow 30s section lifts average view duration

cons.claim: over-optimizing for retention can strip substance into bait
cons.example: jump-cutting every pause until the content feels frantic

failure_modes: edits chase the curve without preserving value
sample too small to be a real signal
acceptance_tests: each recurring drop-off has a diagnosed cause
re-edit guidelines are reusable, not one-off

nodes.definition: Set a sustainable publishing cadence and batch/production system so output stays consistent without burnout.
contradictors: creator who posts in unsustainable bursts then disappears

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when output slips behind cadence or burnout signals appear

pros.claim: consistency compounds reach and trains both audience and algorithm
pros.example: a steady weekly slot builds a returning habit

cons.claim: rigid cadence can force low-quality output to hit a date
cons.example: shipping a weak video just to keep the streak

failure_modes: cadence set beyond sustainable capacity
quality sacrificed to hit the schedule
acceptance_tests: cadence is matched to realistic production capacity
a backlog buffers against missed slots

nodes.definition: Map how a target platform's recommendation signals work and align packaging and metric goals to them.
contradictors: creator who ignores how distribution actually works

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the platform changes ranking signals or the feed mix shifts

pros.claim: aligning to real distribution signals multiplies the reach of the same content
pros.example: optimizing for watch-time over views where the feed rewards it

cons.claim: chasing the algorithm can override audience value and age badly on changes
cons.example: gaming a signal that the platform later down-ranks

failure_modes: strategy built on a stale or guessed algorithm model
optimizing a vanity signal the platform ignores
acceptance_tests: the signal model is dated and revisited on platform changes
optimization targets trace to a real ranking signal

nodes.definition: Adapt aspect ratio, length, pacing, and packaging to each platform's native format and viewing context.
contradictors: creator who reposts identical files everywhere

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a platform changes its preferred format or a format underperforms

pros.claim: native format fit is rewarded by both viewers and feeds
pros.example: vertical captioned shorts outperform cropped landscape clips

cons.claim: over-adapting fragments a recognizable identity across platforms
cons.example: a different voice and look on every platform

failure_modes: one format force-fit to all platforms
adaptation loses the core idea
acceptance_tests: each platform has explicit native format specs
adaptations preserve the core idea

nodes.definition: Decide when and how to participate in trends, sounds, and formats without diluting the niche.
contradictors: creator who chases every trend off-brand

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a trend reach window opens or the niche fit is questionable

pros.claim: timely trend entry can deliver outsized reach to a new audience
pros.example: using a rising sound early surfaces a short to non-followers

cons.claim: off-niche trend chasing attracts the wrong audience and erodes identity
cons.example: a viral dance on a finance channel brings non-converting viewers

failure_modes: trend joined late, after the reach window closes
trend off-brand, attracts the wrong audience
acceptance_tests: each trend is filtered for niche fit before use
trend entry timing is justified, not reflexive

nodes.definition: Optimize titles, descriptions, tags, captions, and chapters for platform and external search discoverability.
contradictors: creator who titles for cleverness over searchability

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when search-driven traffic share or ranking position changes

pros.claim: search surfaces content for months after publish, unlike feed spikes
pros.example: a well-titled tutorial ranks and earns steady evergreen views

cons.claim: keyword-stuffing for search can hurt the human-facing hook
cons.example: a title packed with keywords that no one wants to click

failure_modes: metadata optimized for bots at the cost of click-through
the wrong search intent targeted
acceptance_tests: metadata targets a real search query with demand
the title stays clickable for humans, not just searchable

nodes.definition: Produce short-form vertical content optimized for fast hooks, loops, and high completion rate.
contradictors: creator who crams long-form pacing into shorts

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when short-form completion or reach underperforms the format benchmark

pros.claim: short-form is the dominant discovery surface for new audiences today
pros.example: a strong short brings thousands of non-followers in hours

cons.claim: short-form reach rarely converts to deep loyalty on its own
cons.example: viral shorts with almost no subscriber lift

failure_modes: short uses slow long-form pacing
no loop or payoff to drive completion
acceptance_tests: the first second carries a hook
the edit is built for completion, not just views

nodes.definition: Produce long-form content that builds depth, trust, and watch-time with sustained narrative and value.
contradictors: creator who pads length for the algorithm

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when long-form watch-time or audience-depth metrics decline

pros.claim: long-form builds the trust and watch-time that deepen loyalty and monetization
pros.example: a 15-minute deep dive earns watch-time and a loyal core

cons.claim: long-form is costly and unforgiving of weak pacing
cons.example: a bloated video that loses most viewers in the first third

failure_modes: length padded beyond the value
weak pacing loses viewers early
acceptance_tests: every segment earns its runtime
watch-time is sustained, not just front-loaded

nodes.definition: Design recurring series/franchises that create appointment viewing and a reason to subscribe and return.
contradictors: creator who only makes disconnected one-offs

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a series fails to build returning viewership across episodes

pros.claim: a named series turns scattered views into appointment viewing and subscribes
pros.example: a weekly series viewers wait for, not just stumble on

cons.claim: a weak series concept locks the creator into a failing format
cons.example: committing to a series no one returns for

failure_modes: series concept has no reason to return
episodes drift from the template
acceptance_tests: the series gives an explicit reason to return weekly
episodes share a recognizable template
revisit_triggers: a series fails to retain across episodes

nodes.definition: Use live formats to deepen community, real-time interaction, and platform-favored live signals.
contradictors: creator who goes live with no plan or hook

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when live attendance or interaction quality is low

pros.claim: live builds the strongest real-time bond with the core community
pros.example: a regular live Q&A turns viewers into a community

cons.claim: live is hard to scale, risky in real time, and weak for cold discovery
cons.example: a live with low attendance and no replay value

failure_modes: live has no structure and loses casual viewers
no plan to repurpose the live into VOD
acceptance_tests: live has a planned structure and interaction hook
the live is repurposable into VOD assets

nodes.definition: Convert passive viewers into an interacting community through replies, rituals, and member-driven loops.
contradictors: creator who broadcasts and never engages back

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when engagement rate or community sentiment declines

pros.claim: an engaged community drives retention, feedback, and word-of-mouth growth
pros.example: replying to early comments seeds a culture of interaction

cons.claim: community work is time-intensive and hard to scale as the audience grows
cons.example: reply load that outgrows the creator's capacity

failure_modes: engagement is extractive, not reciprocal
community work ignored until growth stalls
acceptance_tests: there is a repeatable ritual that invites interaction
feedback from community feeds content decisions

nodes.definition: Design calls-to-action and conversion paths that turn attention into subscribers, signups, or revenue.
contradictors: creator who never asks for the next action

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when conversion rate from view to subscribe/signup underperforms

pros.claim: a clear CTA converts earned attention into durable audience and revenue
pros.example: a well-timed subscribe ask lifts conversion meaningfully

cons.claim: too many or mistimed CTAs feel salesy and depress retention
cons.example: three signup pitches inside a five-minute video

failure_modes: CTA absent so attention does not convert
CTA over-asks and breaks trust
acceptance_tests: each piece has one clear, well-timed CTA
the conversion path from view to action is unbroken

nodes.definition: Repurpose one core asset into multiple platform-native pieces to maximize reach per unit of production.
contradictors: creator who makes everything from scratch each time

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when repurposing yield per asset drops or feels mechanical

pros.claim: repurposing multiplies reach and cadence without multiplying production cost
pros.example: one long video yields a week of shorts and posts

cons.claim: lazy repurposing posts non-native clips that underperform
cons.example: cropping a landscape clip into a vertical with bars

failure_modes: derivatives not adapted to each platform
repurposing dilutes the core message
acceptance_tests: each derivative is natively reformatted, not just re-uploaded
repurposing keeps the core message intact

nodes.definition: Run a measurement loop that turns reach, retention, and conversion data into the next strategy iteration.
contradictors: creator who posts on vibes and never measures

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when metrics diverge from plan or an experiment concludes

pros.claim: a measurement loop replaces guessing with compounding learning
pros.example: a/b testing thumbnails turns click-through into a steerable metric

cons.claim: vanity metrics or small samples mislead the whole strategy
cons.example: chasing views while subscribers and revenue stall

failure_modes: optimizing vanity metrics over real goals
decisions made on samples too small to trust
acceptance_tests: each tracked metric ties to a stated goal
every iteration cites the metric that drove it

nodes.definition: Gate publishing on hook, format-fit, value-promise, CTA, and metadata checks before content goes live.
contradictors: creator who publishes without any review pass

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a published piece bypasses or fails a readiness check

pros.claim: a readiness gate prevents publishing avoidable misses that are costly to undo
pros.example: catching a broken hook or wrong aspect ratio before it goes live

cons.claim: a heavy gate can slow cadence if over-engineered
cons.example: a checklist so long it delays every post

failure_modes: content published before checks pass
gate so heavy it blocks cadence
acceptance_tests: no piece publishes before hook/format/value/CTA/metadata checks pass
go/no-go is recorded for high-stakes posts
revisit_triggers: a published piece fails a check

edges.why_related: the persona is built for the chosen niche
edges.risk_of_conflict: wrong niche yields a wrong persona
edges.example: picking the niche before profiling the viewer
edges.resolution_rule: fix the niche before building the persona

edges.why_related: the value promise is defined for the profiled audience
edges.benefit_of_coupling: promise speaks to a real viewer
edges.risk_of_conflict: a fictional persona yields a hollow promise
edges.example: writing the promise after knowing the viewer
edges.resolution_rule: define the persona before the value loop

edges.why_related: pillars are chosen around the persona's problems
edges.benefit_of_coupling: pillars map to real audience needs
edges.risk_of_conflict: pillars drift without a persona
edges.example: deriving pillars from the persona's problem list
edges.resolution_rule: profile the audience before fixing pillars

edges.why_related: pillars must deliver the value promise
edges.risk_of_conflict: pillars unrelated to the promise break the loop
edges.example: aligning each pillar to the value loop
edges.resolution_rule: set the promise before the pillars

edges.why_related: hooks use the persona's language and pains
edges.benefit_of_coupling: hooks land in the viewer's words
edges.risk_of_conflict: generic hooks miss a specific viewer
edges.example: writing hooks in the audience's own phrasing
edges.resolution_rule: know the persona before writing hooks

edges.why_related: the story must pay off the hook's promise
edges.risk_of_conflict: a story that abandons the hook loses trust
edges.example: structuring the body to deliver the hook
edges.resolution_rule: design the hook before the story arc

edges.why_related: retention diagnosis acts on the story's pacing
edges.risk_of_conflict: with no story there is nothing to diagnose
edges.example: reading the curve against the story structure
edges.resolution_rule: build the story before tuning retention

edges.why_related: platform choice follows where the audience watches
edges.benefit_of_coupling: algorithm work targets the right platform
edges.risk_of_conflict: optimizing a platform the audience ignores
edges.example: modeling the algorithm of the audience's platform
edges.resolution_rule: profile the audience before modeling the algorithm

edges.why_related: format specs derive from platform signals
edges.benefit_of_coupling: format fits what the feed rewards
edges.risk_of_conflict: format mismatched to the platform underperforms
edges.example: setting format specs from the signal model
edges.resolution_rule: model the algorithm before fixing formats

edges.why_related: the cadence is fed by the pillar backlog
edges.benefit_of_coupling: cadence draws on a planned backlog
edges.risk_of_conflict: cadence without a backlog forces filler
edges.example: scheduling output from the pillar backlog
edges.resolution_rule: define pillars before committing a cadence

edges.why_related: pillars bound which trends fit the niche
edges.risk_of_conflict: unfiltered trends pull off-niche
edges.example: filtering trends through the pillar fit
edges.resolution_rule: pillars gate which trends are allowed

edges.why_related: search optimization targets pillar topics
edges.risk_of_conflict: SEO scattered across off-pillar topics
edges.example: mapping keywords to pillars
edges.resolution_rule: fix pillars before optimizing discovery

edges.why_related: short-form production follows the platform's format specs
edges.risk_of_conflict: off-spec shorts underperform
edges.example: producing shorts to the platform spec
edges.resolution_rule: fix format specs before producing shorts

edges.why_related: short-form lives or dies on the first-second hook
edges.benefit_of_coupling: shorts open with a tested hook
edges.risk_of_conflict: a weak open kills short completion
edges.example: front-loading the hook in shorts
edges.resolution_rule: design the hook before producing shorts

edges.why_related: long-form production follows platform format norms
edges.risk_of_conflict: off-norm long-form loses watch-time
edges.example: producing long-form to platform norms
edges.resolution_rule: fix format specs before producing long-form

edges.why_related: long-form depends on sustained narrative structure
edges.risk_of_conflict: weak structure collapses long-form
edges.example: building long-form on the story outline
edges.resolution_rule: structure the story before long-form production

edges.why_related: series are built from recurring pillars
edges.risk_of_conflict: series with no pillar lack a spine
edges.example: designing series around a pillar
edges.resolution_rule: fix pillars before designing series

edges.why_related: a series gives the value loop a repeatable container
edges.risk_of_conflict: series without the loop give no reason to return
edges.example: anchoring the series to the return loop
edges.resolution_rule: define the value loop before the series

edges.why_related: community forms around a clear, repeated promise
edges.risk_of_conflict: no promise, no community to rally
edges.example: building rituals around the value loop
edges.resolution_rule: define the promise before community rituals

edges.why_related: live deepens an already-engaged community
edges.risk_of_conflict: live with no community is empty
edges.example: planning live around the community
edges.resolution_rule: build community before relying on live

edges.why_related: the CTA converts the value promise into an action
edges.risk_of_conflict: CTA without a promise feels empty
edges.example: tying the CTA to the value loop
edges.resolution_rule: define the promise before designing the CTA

edges.why_related: repurposing reformats to each platform's specs
edges.risk_of_conflict: off-spec repurposing underperforms
edges.example: reformatting assets to each platform spec
edges.resolution_rule: fix format specs before repurposing

edges.why_related: repurposing helps sustain the committed cadence
edges.risk_of_conflict: without repurposing cadence is harder to keep
edges.example: scheduling derivatives into the calendar
edges.resolution_rule: set cadence, then use repurposing to sustain it

edges.why_related: the analytics loop consumes retention diagnoses
edges.benefit_of_coupling: the loop learns from the curve
edges.risk_of_conflict: no retention data weakens the loop
edges.example: feeding retention findings into iteration
edges.resolution_rule: diagnose retention before the analytics loop

edges.why_related: the loop measures whether CTAs convert
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmeasured CTAs cannot improve
edges.example: tracking conversion in the loop
edges.resolution_rule: design CTAs before measuring conversion

edges.why_related: the loop tests whether the promise drives return
edges.risk_of_conflict: an unmeasured promise cannot be tuned
edges.example: measuring return against the promise
edges.resolution_rule: define the promise before measuring it

edges.why_related: the gate checks the hook before publish
edges.benefit_of_coupling: the gate enforces a strong hook
edges.risk_of_conflict: a weak hook slips through without the gate
edges.example: verifying the hook at the gate
edges.resolution_rule: design the hook before the readiness gate

edges.why_related: the gate checks format-fit before publish
edges.risk_of_conflict: off-format posts slip through without the gate
edges.example: verifying format-fit at the gate
edges.resolution_rule: fix format specs before the readiness gate

edges.why_related: the gate checks metadata before publish
edges.risk_of_conflict: unoptimized metadata slips through without the gate
edges.example: verifying metadata at the gate
edges.resolution_rule: optimize metadata before the readiness gate

edges.why_related: the gate checks the CTA before publish
edges.benefit_of_coupling: the gate enforces a clear CTA
edges.risk_of_conflict: a missing CTA slips through without the gate
edges.example: verifying the CTA at the gate
edges.resolution_rule: design the CTA before the readiness gate

edges.why_related: analytics can trigger revisiting the niche thesis
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring data freezes a failing niche
edges.example: data showing the niche has no durable demand
edges.resolution_rule: stop when niche metrics stabilize for two cycles

edges.why_related: analytics can trigger re-balancing pillars
edges.risk_of_conflict: clinging to a dead pillar wastes cadence
edges.example: a pillar that consistently underperforms
edges.resolution_rule: stop when pillar performance is within target

edges.why_related: analytics can trigger re-testing hooks
edges.risk_of_conflict: stale hooks decay click-through
edges.example: click-through falling below benchmark
edges.resolution_rule: stop when click-through recovers to target

edges.why_related: hitting a cadence competes with polishing each piece's retention
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension keeps both shipping and quality honest
edges.risk_of_conflict: cadence pressure ships unpolished pieces
edges.example: skipping retention edits to meet a deadline
edges.resolution_rule: quality floor dominates; cadence may not publish below the floor

edges.why_related: chasing reach via trends competes with niche focus
edges.risk_of_conflict: off-niche trends attract the wrong audience
edges.example: a viral but off-niche trend tempting the creator
edges.resolution_rule: niche fit dominates; off-niche trends are declined

edges.why_related: optimizing for the algorithm competes with the audience value promise
edges.risk_of_conflict: algorithm-chasing erodes the promise
edges.example: gaming a signal at the cost of viewer value
edges.resolution_rule: audience value dominates; algorithm tactics may not break the promise

edges.why_related: limited production capacity splits between short and long formats
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension forces a deliberate format mix
edges.risk_of_conflict: splitting effort makes both formats mediocre
edges.example: trying to do daily shorts and weekly long-form at once
edges.resolution_rule: the format mix is set by where the audience and goals are, not by impulse

edges.why_related: adding CTAs competes with sustaining watch-time
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension keeps CTAs from harming retention
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-asking depresses retention
edges.example: stacking signup pitches inside the video
edges.resolution_rule: retention floor dominates; CTAs may not break the retention floor

edges.why_related: community engagement time competes with production cadence
edges.risk_of_conflict: reply load crowds out producing content
edges.example: spending all week replying and missing the upload
edges.resolution_rule: allocate capacity explicitly; neither starves the other

edges.why_related: both turn a core idea into platform-native short pieces
edges.risk_of_conflict: conflating them hides that repurposing reuses an existing asset
edges.example: a short produced fresh vs a short cut from a long video
edges.resolution_rule: treat as distinct: production creates, repurposing derives

conflict_axes.trigger: a high-reach trend pulls away from the focused niche
resolution_order: check trend fit against the niche thesis
participate only if it serves the target audience
decline or re-angle off-niche trends
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: niche fit dominates; reach that brings the wrong audience is declined
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a trend would attract a non-converting audience at scale
conflict_axes.example: a viral off-topic format that spikes views but not subscribers

conflict_axes.trigger: optimizing a ranking signal competes with the viewer value promise
resolution_order: state the audience value first
optimize only tactics that do not break the promise
drop tactics that degrade trust
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: audience value dominates; algorithm tactics may not falsify or cheapen the promise
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a tactic boosts a metric while eroding viewer trust
conflict_axes.example: title gaming that lifts clicks but burns credibility

conflict_axes.trigger: hitting a publishing date competes with polishing each piece
resolution_order: set a minimum quality floor
ship on cadence only above the floor
slip the date rather than publish below the floor
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the quality floor dominates; cadence may not force sub-floor output
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if meeting a date requires publishing below the quality floor
conflict_axes.example: shipping a weak video just to keep a streak

conflict_axes.trigger: limited capacity must be split between reach and depth formats
resolution_order: set the format mix from the audience goal
allocate capacity deliberately
avoid doing both badly
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the goal (reach now vs depth/loyalty) sets the mix; impulse does not
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if both formats become mediocre from split effort
conflict_axes.example: daily shorts plus weekly long-form with no slack

conflict_axes.trigger: adding conversion asks competes with sustaining watch-time
resolution_order: limit to one primary CTA
place it where retention can absorb it
cut asks that depress the curve
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the retention floor dominates; CTAs may not break it
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a CTA placement measurably drops retention
conflict_axes.example: three signup pitches inside a short video

conflict_axes.trigger: trends reward fast entry but the gate enforces review
resolution_order: pre-clear trend templates so review is fast
keep the minimum gate even under time pressure
never skip the hook/format checks
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the minimum readiness gate dominates; speed may compress review but not remove it
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if speed pressure tempts publishing without any review
conflict_axes.example: posting a trend clip with the wrong aspect ratio to be first

conflict_axes.trigger: engagement time competes with time to produce content
resolution_order: budget fixed time for community
protect production capacity
scale community via rituals and moderation, not unbounded replies
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: neither starves the other; capacity is allocated explicitly with a cap on each
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if reply load causes missed uploads or vice versa
conflict_axes.example: spending the whole week in comments and missing the post

conflict_axes.trigger: a specific persona competes with chasing broad mass appeal
resolution_order: serve the specific persona first
broaden only where it still fits the persona
reject broad ideas that betray the persona
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the specific persona dominates; broad reach is pursued only when persona-consistent
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if broadening for reach would alienate the core audience
conflict_axes.example: watering down a niche channel to chase general virality

edge_cases.trigger: content gradually spreads beyond the niche
edge_cases.failure_mode: unfocused channel with no clear audience
edge_cases.example: a tech channel slowly becomes a general vlog
edge_cases.detection_method: audit recent pieces against the niche thesis

edge_cases.trigger: the hook promises more than the body delivers
edge_cases.failure_mode: high click-through but collapsing retention and trust
edge_cases.example: a clickbait title the video never pays off
resolution: align the hook to the actual payoff

edge_cases.trigger: strategy optimizes views while real goals stall
edge_cases.failure_mode: growth on paper, no durable audience or revenue
edge_cases.example: celebrating viral views while subscribers and revenue are flat
edge_cases.detection_method: check each tracked metric maps to a stated goal

edge_cases.trigger: tactics chase a signal that the platform later down-ranks
edge_cases.failure_mode: reach collapses on an algorithm change
edge_cases.example: building a channel on one exploited loophole
edge_cases.detection_method: check optimization targets trace to durable value, not loopholes

edge_cases.trigger: an off-niche trend brings the wrong audience
edge_cases.example: a viral dance on a finance channel
edge_cases.detection_method: check the new audience matches the persona

edge_cases.trigger: derivatives are reposted without native reformatting
edge_cases.failure_mode: cross-posted clips underperform on every platform
edge_cases.example: a letterboxed landscape clip posted as a short
edge_cases.detection_method: check each derivative against the platform format spec

edge_cases.trigger: cadence is set beyond sustainable capacity
edge_cases.example: committing to daily uploads solo and quitting in a month
edge_cases.detection_method: check cadence against realistic capacity and backlog

edge_cases.trigger: a piece is published before readiness checks pass
edge_cases.example: publishing with a broken hook or wrong aspect ratio
edge_cases.detection_method: check the gate ran before the post went live

edge_cases.trigger: pieces have no consistent reason to return
edge_cases.failure_mode: viral spikes with flat subscriber growth
edge_cases.example: high views but no subscriber lift
edge_cases.detection_method: check a stated, kept promise exists across recent pieces

edge_cases.trigger: metadata optimized for bots at the cost of human click-through
edge_cases.failure_mode: searchable titles no human wants to click
edge_cases.example: a keyword-stuffed title with low click-through
edge_cases.detection_method: check the title is both searchable and clickable

edge_cases.trigger: a committed series fails to retain across episodes
edge_cases.example: episode 4 of a series no one returns for
resolution: extract the working element into a new format

workflow.objective: fix the niche and the target viewer
entry_criteria: a creator goal to build an audience exists
acceptance_tests: niche names audience and transformation in one sentence
persona is grounded in real data
workflow.do_first_because: everything downstream inherits the niche and viewer; a wrong base reworks the whole channel

workflow.objective: define the value promise and content pillars
acceptance_tests: the promise is one sentence kept every piece
each pillar maps to an audience problem
workflow.do_first_because: the promise and pillars steer every later content and format choice

workflow.objective: model the platform and set format and discovery rules
acceptance_tests: optimization targets trace to real signals
each platform has explicit native format specs
workflow.do_first_because: format and packaging must fit how distribution actually works before producing

workflow.objective: design the hook and narrative structure for a piece
entry_criteria: a content idea selected from a pillar
acceptance_tests: the hook names a payoff it can keep
each segment advances one through-line
workflow.do_first_because: the hook and structure determine whether produced content holds attention at all

workflow.objective: produce the content in the chosen format
acceptance_tests: assets match the platform format spec
the edit is built for completion/watch-time
workflow.do_first_because: production must follow the approved creative and format rules to avoid re-shoots

workflow.objective: add conversion paths and plan reach and repurposing
acceptance_tests: each piece has one clear well-timed CTA
each trend passes the niche-fit filter
workflow.do_first_because: conversion and reach are planned on finished assets, not retrofitted after publish

workflow.objective: run pre-publish checks and a go/no-go
acceptance_tests: all readiness checks pass
quality is at or above the floor
workflow.do_first_because: a readiness gate prevents costly public misses that are hard to undo

workflow.objective: publish, engage the community, and run live touchpoints
acceptance_tests: a repeatable engagement ritual is live
community time stays within its capacity cap
workflow.do_first_because: engagement compounds reach and loyalty only after content is live

workflow.objective: measure outcomes and feed the next iteration
acceptance_tests: each tracked metric ties to a stated goal
decisions rest on sufficient samples
workflow.do_first_because: measurement closes the loop and steers the next cycle instead of guessing

priority_rationale.notes: root focus the whole channel inherits
viewer model every later choice depends on
the promise that makes audience compound
distribution model that format fit depends on
high-risk attention gate for every piece
the structure retention work acts on
the conversion step that turns reach into audience
opportunistic reach, gated by niche fit
closes the loop and steers iteration
final high-risk gate before public release

dominance_rules.trigger: an algorithm tactic would erode the audience value promise
dominance_rules.rule: audience value dominates over algorithm optimization
dominance_rules.required_action: drop any tactic that falsifies or cheapens the promise
dominance_rules.example: removing a clickbait title that beats the metric but burns trust

dominance_rules.trigger: an off-niche trend offers reach that brings the wrong audience
dominance_rules.rule: niche fit dominates over raw reach
dominance_rules.required_action: decline or re-angle trends that fail the niche-fit filter

dominance_rules.trigger: meeting a date would require publishing below the quality floor
dominance_rules.rule: the quality floor dominates over cadence
dominance_rules.required_action: slip the date rather than publish below the floor
dominance_rules.example: delaying an upload that is not ready

dominance_rules.trigger: a conversion ask measurably depresses watch-time
dominance_rules.rule: the retention floor dominates over conversion asks
dominance_rules.required_action: limit to one well-placed CTA and cut the rest
dominance_rules.example: removing extra signup pitches that drop retention

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-risk node would ship without review to save time
dominance_rules.required_action: run the readiness gate before publishing high-risk pieces
dominance_rules.example: not skipping the gate to be first on a trend

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node is unfinished because an upstream prerequisite is not done
dominance_rules.rule: dependency order dominates over value order
dominance_rules.required_action: complete the prerequisite before finalizing the dependent node
dominance_rules.example: fixing the persona before writing hooks

dominance_rules.trigger: a number is stated with false precision beyond its evidence
dominance_rules.rule: the evidence label dominates over numeric precision
dominance_rules.required_action: keep values heuristic when no measured data exists
dominance_rules.example: not labeling a guessed retention rate as observed

dominance_rules.trigger: a piece would be locked before readiness checks pass
dominance_rules.required_action: do not lock or publish before the gate passes
dominance_rules.example: blocking a lock until the checklist clears

dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible or high-stakes publishing decision arises
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates over automation for irreversible decisions
dominance_rules.required_action: require human go/no-go on high-stakes posts
dominance_rules.example: a person approving a sensitive public statement

dominance_rules.trigger: a new object is created without a traceable source or rationale
dominance_rules.rule: traceability dominates over unsupported object creation
dominance_rules.required_action: tie each object to a source and competency question
dominance_rules.example: not adding a metric with no evidence ref

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the niche before profiling the persona
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a persona built for the wrong niche is reworked wholesale
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: the persona changes after the niche is redefined
anti_rework_rules.example: profiling viewers before choosing a niche

anti_rework_rules.rule: define the persona before the value promise
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a promise for a fictional viewer must be rebuilt
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: the promise is rewritten after the persona is corrected
anti_rework_rules.example: writing a promise before knowing the viewer

anti_rework_rules.rule: set the value promise before the pillars
anti_rework_rules.rationale: pillars that do not serve the promise are scrapped
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: pillars are re-cut after the promise is clarified
anti_rework_rules.example: choosing pillars with no stated promise

anti_rework_rules.rule: model the platform algorithm before fixing formats
anti_rework_rules.rationale: formats set against the wrong signals are redone
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: format specs change after the signal model is built
anti_rework_rules.example: fixing aspect/length before knowing the platform

anti_rework_rules.rule: approve the hook and structure before producing
anti_rework_rules.rationale: producing before a hook means re-shoots and re-edits
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: the edit is reworked after the hook is rethought
anti_rework_rules.example: editing a full video around a weak opener

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix per-platform format specs before repurposing
anti_rework_rules.rationale: non-native derivatives underperform and are redone

anti_rework_rules.rule: design the CTA before the readiness gate
anti_rework_rules.rationale: publishing without a CTA wastes earned attention
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: the post is edited post-publish to add a CTA

anti_rework_rules.rule: pass the readiness gate before publishing
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a public miss is far costlier than a pre-publish check
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: content is unpublished or reposted after a caught error
anti_rework_rules.example: posting with the wrong aspect ratio

anti_rework_rules.rationale: pivoting on noise wastes the compounding already built
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: strategy is reversed again the next week
anti_rework_rules.example: killing a niche after two low-view posts

anti_rework_rules.rule: size capacity before committing a cadence
anti_rework_rules.rationale: an unsustainable cadence collapses the whole channel
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: uploads are missed and the schedule is reset

iteration_protocol.trigger: a validator check or a published-piece metric fails
iteration_protocol.detection: compare validation_report and analytics against thresholds
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no failing checks or under-threshold metrics remain

iteration_protocol.trigger: multiple defects compete for limited attention
iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk x reach
action: score defects by risk and reach
acceptance_tests: highest risk-reach defect is first

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect touches a high-coupling node
iteration_protocol.detection: trace edges from the defect node
acceptance_tests: all dependents of the defect are listed

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is ready to fix
action: apply the fix at the owning subsystem
acceptance_tests: the targeted defect no longer reproduces

iteration_protocol.trigger: a repair changed a locked or high-coupling component
iteration_protocol.detection: re-run the validator and affected gates
acceptance_tests: no new failures introduced

iteration_protocol.trigger: new analytics shift a node's importance
action: re-sort the affected slice of priority_order
acceptance_tests: priority changes trace to a metric
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: posterior change below the revisit delta

iteration_protocol.trigger: an upstream node changed after dependents were locked
iteration_protocol.detection: detect upstream change on locked dependents
acceptance_tests: all affected dependents downgraded
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no locked dependent has a changed upstream

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is irreversible, high-risk, or sensitive
acceptance_tests: a human decision is recorded before action
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: the escalated item has a recorded decision

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new cycle could regress a prior result
iteration_protocol.detection: compare against the previous cycle's metrics and validation
acceptance_tests: no metric or check regressed unexplained

handling of sensitive or controversial topics

expected_properties: content traces to one niche thesis

change_triggers: a series is added or retired
version_increment_rules: increment on any hard-locked strategy change
increment when formulas or metric weights change
lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade dependents when an upstream node changes
downgrade on a failed readiness gate
downgrade when an evidence label is revised
